claims: Keppra tablets/solution treat partial-onset seizures from age 1 month, as monotherapy or adjunctive therapy. Adjunctive indications are myoclonic seizures with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy from age 12 and primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures with idiopathic generalized epilepsy from age 6. IV Keppra has these indications only as an alternative when oral administration is temporarily infeasible; clinical IV experience beyond 4 days is lacking.

Keppra XR treats partial-onset seizures from age 12; its standard starting regimen is specified for weight≥ 50 kg. Elepsia XR is adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures from age 12. Spritam treats partial-onset seizures from age 4 with weight> 20 kg, and adjunctively treats JME myoclonic seizures from 12 and idiopathic generalized tonic-clonic seizures from 6; Spritam is not recommended in children weighing≤ 20 kg. No status-epilepticus loading regimen is supplied by these labels.

These are adult tables using estimated CrCl adjusted for body surface area, not an interchangeable unadjusted eGFR or pediatric algorithm. Printed mild/moderate ranges share 50; the treating team must resolve boundary classification and individualized dose. Elepsia XR provides only> 80: 1000–3000 mg daily and 50–80: 1000–2000 mg daily; it is not recommended for moderate/severe impairment, and dialysis requires an IR alternative. Pediatric renal adjustment data are not supplied in IV labeling; consult pediatric specialists rather than applying adult tables.

IR Keppra may be taken with or without food; swallow tablets whole without chewing/crushing. Use 100 mg/mL oral solution for pediatric weight≤ 20 kg with a calibrated oral measuring device; prescribed mg per dose divided by 100 gives mL per dose. XR tablets must remain whole: never chew, break or crush Keppra XR; never split/cut Elepsia XR. Spritam uses whole tablets only: peel foil with dry hands, place one on tongue and take a sip of liquid, then swallow after dispersal; do not swallow intact. A whole-tablet cup dispersion is also allowed, followed by a residue rinse. Do not independently substitute IR/XR schedules.

assertionMap.card: IV concentrate and Spritam tube administration
claims: For temporary IV Keppra substitution, match the IR oral total daily dose and frequency in either direction. Dilute selected 100 mg/mL concentrate in 100 mL compatible fluid for adults; if smaller volume is required, final concentration must not exceed 15 mg/mL. Infuse over 15 minutes, not an inferred IV-push/loading regimen. Compatible diluents are 0.9% saline, lactated Ringer’s and 5% dextrose. Spritam’s selected tube method is only for NG/G tubes French 10–14: disperse prescribed whole tablets in about 10 mL room-temperature water, administer immediately with 10 mL oral catheter-tip syringe, then twice add 10 mL water to the cup, swirl residue and flush through the same tube. Verify package method and fluid allowances.

Monitor aggression, agitation, irritability, depression, psychosis and suicidal thoughts/behavior; seek prompt assessment for new/worsening symptoms and urgent care for self-harm risk. Antiseizure-drug pooled data do not establish a personal risk estimate.
Somnolence, fatigue, dizziness and incoordination can impair driving and increase injury risk. Avoid hazardous activities until effects are known.
Anaphylaxis/angioedema can occur after the first or later dose; discontinue and seek immediate care. Permanently stop if a clear alternative cause cannot be established.
SJS/TEN and serious rash can occur. Discontinue at the first rash unless clearly unrelated; suspected SJS/TEN must not be rechallenged.

DRESS can involve fever, rash, nodes/facial swelling and liver, kidney, blood or cardiac injury. Early fever/nodes may precede rash; evaluate immediately and discontinue if no alternative cause is established.
Generally taper withdrawal to reduce more frequent seizures/status epilepticus; serious adverse reactions may justify rapid medically supervised cessation.
Blood-cell abnormalities include cytopenias; obtain CBC for significant weakness, fever, recurrent infections or coagulation symptoms. Monitor diastolic BP in age 1 month to< 4 years.
Assess renal function for accumulation and correct product-specific dose. Pregnancy may lower drug levels; monitor through postpartum, especially after dose changes.
Known hypersensitivity to levetiracetam; anaphylaxis and angioedema have occurred. Verify excipients/formulation history when selecting a product.

The selected levetiracetam labels have no boxed warning. Suicidal thoughts/behavior, severe hypersensitivity and withdrawal-related seizures remain important warnings; absence of a box does not remove the need for monitoring.

Common reports include somnolence, weakness/fatigue, dizziness and infection; pediatric reports also include aggression, irritability, appetite reduction and nasal symptoms. Patterns/rates depend on age, seizure indication and formulation trials. Postmarketing reports include cytopenias, severe skin/systemic allergy, liver injury, kidney injury, hyponatremia, movement symptoms and seizure worsening. Overdose can cause agitation/aggression, depressed consciousness, respiratory depression or coma. No specific antidote is known; obtain urgent medical/Poison Help advice, protect airway and monitor clinically. Clinicians may consider hemodialysis, which removes about 50% in 4 hours; do not attempt home emesis.

Levetiracetam is not substantially CYP-metabolized and has low protein binding. Label studies found no relevant interaction with phenytoin, valproate, warfarin, digoxin or the studied ethinyl-estradiol/levonorgestrel contraceptive. This is not proof of no interaction with every drug or hormone product. Pediatric enzyme-inducing antiseizure co-treatment increased apparent clearance about 22%, without a recommended automatic adjustment.

Probenecid reduces clearance of the inactive major metabolite and raises its peak, while parent levetiracetam pharmacokinetics were unchanged; the reverse effect was not studied. Review sedating agents in patients with somnolence/incoordination and monitor clinical impairment. IV compatibility is product-specific: selected Keppra supports lorazepam, diazepam and valproate sodium mixtures, with no compatibility data for other antiseizure agents; do not infer compatibility or stability of another premix.

Renal clearance falls with impairment; use the appropriate adult renal regimen, including IR postdialysis supplement. Elepsia XR has additional restrictions. Older adults need careful selection and renal monitoring. Keppra PK studies found no hepatic-only dose adjustment needed; severe hepatic disease reduced total clearance largely through reduced renal clearance, so still assess kidney function. Other product populations must follow their exact labels.

Prolonged human experience and registry/literature data have not identified a major-birth-defect or miscarriage association, but cannot establish absence of risk; animal developmental toxicity is reported. Levels may fall during pregnancy, especially third trimester; monitor response/levels and continue close postpartum review if dose changed. Discuss pregnancy registry enrollment and the risk of uncontrolled seizures before altering treatment. Levetiracetam enters human milk; selected label lacks infant-effect/milk-production data. Weigh maternal need, feeding benefits and potential infant risk.

IR/IV partial-onset use begins at 1 month; other seizure types and products have different ages. Keppra IR solution is required at weight≤ 20 kg; Spritam is not recommended in children≤ 20 kg despite a dosing-table heading beginning at 20. Keppra XR’s specified standard regimen requires age≥ 12 and weight≥ 50 kg; Elepsia XR is not indicated below 12. Infants/young children need behavioral, growth/development and age-specific BP assessment, with no invented pediatric renal algorithm.

The antiseizure mechanism is not fully defined. Binding to synaptic-vesicle protein SV2A may contribute to altered vesicle exocytosis and antiseizure activity; the exact molecular significance remains uncertain.
IR absorption
Fast oral absorption; peak about 1 hour fasting,100% bioavailability. IR tablets and oral solution are bioequivalent; food delays/reduces peak without reducing extent.
XR absorption
Keppra XR peak about 4 hours; food can further delay it. A comparable daily exposure does not justify independent schedule substitution.
Binding / metabolism
< 10% protein-bound. Major inactive metabolite arises from non-CYP enzymatic hydrolysis.
Elimination / half-life
Approximately 66% excreted unchanged renally; adult half-life about 7 ± 1 hour, prolonged with renal impairment/older age.
Treatment implication
Renal function and formulation drive dosing; pregnancy and younger age can change clearance.

Track seizure control, adherence, mood/behavior, sedation and coordination. Assess renal function initially and as clinically warranted; recalculate adult BSA-adjusted CrCl and review weight-based pediatric doses. CBC is symptom-triggered per warning; monitor young-child diastolic BP. Pregnancy/postpartum warrants close seizure/level monitoring when appropriate. No universal therapeutic concentration or routine laboratory interval is supplied by these labels.

Do not stop or change IR/XR frequency independently. Report self-harm thoughts, major behavioral changes, fever/nodes/rash or allergic swelling/breathing difficulty urgently. Delay driving/hazardous activities until effects and seizure restrictions are understood. Use a calibrated oral syringe for solution; verify 100 mg/mL and per-dose mL. Follow whole-tablet restrictions and Spritam’s liquid-assisted dispersal. Discuss pregnancy/feeding plans, keep follow-up visits and check the medicine name/strength when refilled.

claims: Keppra IR/solution/XR, selected IV and Spritam: store at 25°C, excursions 15–30°C. Elepsia XR: 20–25°C, excursions 15–30°C; dispense tight/light-resistant. Keep Spritam protected in intact blister until use, peel rather than push, and administer dispersions immediately. Selected IV diluted solution may be held no more than 4 hours at 15–30°C; inspect for particles/discoloration and discard unused vial contents. Follow pharmacist-prepared product requirements rather than extending concentrate stability to another premix.

claims: An antiseizure medicine with immediate-release, extended-release, oral-suspension-tablet and temporary IV options. Indications, age/weight limits, renal regimens and administration depend on the exact product.

New suicidal thoughts, aggression/psychosis or serious rash/systemic allergy require prompt assessment. Gradual withdrawal ordinarily reduces increased seizures/status epilepticus, but serious reactions may require urgent discontinuation under medical supervision.
Therapeutic class
Antiseizure medicine · SV2A-binding agent
Representative formulation
Keppra 500 mg immediate-release oral tablet
Reference focus
U.S. IR/solution, IV, Keppra XR, Spritam and Elepsia XR

exclusions: Other manufacturers/premixes, non-U.S. marketing, off-label emergency loading or other unverified algorithms; no stock availability inference.

gaps.topic: Renal boundaries and pediatric renal data
gaps.finding: Printed adult tables share50mL/min/1.73m² between mild/moderate groups. Pediatric IV renal-adjustment information is unavailable; selected KeppraXR standard regimen requires≥ 50kg.
gaps.resolution: Ranges reproduced as printed and boundary choice explicitly clinician-dependent, no unsupported numeric automatic algorithm. No adult renal table transferred to children or< 50kg XR adolescent starting dose invented.

gaps.topic: Selected IV and XR transition scope
gaps.resolution: IV label provides temporary IR-equivalent dose/frequency,15-minute diluted infusion and no experience> 4days; no status-epilepticus loading or IV push regimen invented. IR/XR equal-dose clinical effectiveness not assumed; dialysis XR algorithm not invented.
